text.title: AI Overview Presence Tracker Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every AI Overview Presence Tracker application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: The tracked query set MUST contain at least 20 queries, each mapped to one target URL on the tracked domain, and MUST stay fixed for the whole 8-week window. Adding or removing queries MUST start a new query-set version with its own window; a report MUST NOT mix rows from two versions in one trend.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope: at least 20 indexed pages targeting AIO queries, 8-week trend view; widely established rank-tracking practice

rule.rationale: An AIO presence rate over a set whose membership changed mid-window measures the editing of the list, not Google. Twenty is the floor at which a one-query change moves the rate by less than five points.

rule.statement: Every weekly observation MUST be a row with `query`, `observed_at` (date), `aio_present` (boolean), `citations` (list of URLs, empty when no panel), `our_domain_cited` (boolean), `selected_snippet` (text or null) and `panel_position` (integer or null). `citations`, `selected_snippet` and `panel_position` MUST be null or empty only when `aio_present` is false; a present panel with an unrecorded citation list MUST be logged as a scrape failure, not as zero citations.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope: per-query fields aio_present, citations, our_domain_cited, selected_snippet, panel_position

rule.rationale: "No citations" and "did not capture citations" are different facts; conflating them produces a citation rate that falls every time the scraper has a bad week. Typing the fields keeps the downstream retrofit ranking honest.

rule.statement: All scrapes in a window MUST use one fixed country, language, device type and a logged-out, personalisation-free session, recorded in the report. Changing any of these MUST start a new series. AI Overview availability MUST be checked for the chosen country and language before the window starts.

rationale.source: Google Search Central, 'AI features and your website' (AI Overviews availability varies by country and language)

rule.rationale: AI Overviews roll out by market and language and differ between mobile and desktop; a mobile-US scrape one week and a desktop-UK scrape the next produce a presence swing that has nothing to do with the tracked pages.

rule.statement: Each query MUST be scraped once per week on the same weekday, within a 48-hour tolerance. A week whose scrape failed for a query MUST be recorded as missing and MUST NOT be filled from the adjacent weeks; presence rates for that week MUST use the reduced denominator and say so.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope: weekly Search Console and analytics review cadence; widely established time-series practice

rule.rationale: AIO panels appear and disappear day to day. Interpolating a missing week invents a stability the SERP does not have, and the 8-week retrofit priority then rests on rows that were never observed.

rule.statement: `our_domain_cited` MUST be true only when at least one URL in `citations` has a registrable domain equal to the tracked domain (subdomains included only when listed in the tracker config). A brand mention in `selected_snippet` text, a citation of a syndicated copy, or a competitor page quoting ours MUST NOT set it to true.

rationale.source: widely established web-analytics practice for referrer and citation attribution

rule.rationale: The finding the report exists to produce is "our page is cited or it is not". Counting brand mentions inflates the citation rate and hides exactly the queries where a retrofit would earn the link.

rule.statement: `metrics[]` MUST include, per week and for the window, `aio_presence_rate` (queries with `aio_present` true ÷ queries observed, `unit: ratio`), `our_citation_rate` (queries with `our_domain_cited` true ÷ queries with `aio_present` true, `unit: ratio`) and `median_panel_position` (`unit: count`, over present panels). Rates MUST be ratios between 0 and 1; a metric with the wrong denominator MUST be rejected.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope; widely established SEO-reporting practice

rule.rationale: Citation rate over all queries, rather than over queries with a panel, drops whenever panels disappear and rises whenever they return, and the team reads it as their pages gaining or losing citations. The denominators have to be written down.

rule.statement: Findings MUST NOT attribute Search Console click or impression changes to AI Overview presence or citation. Search Console data MAY be shown alongside presence data for the same query, but the finding MUST describe it as co-occurring, and a causal claim MUST be rejected.

rationale.source: Google Search Console documentation: AI Overview impressions and clicks are counted inside the Web search type with no separate filter

rule.rationale: Because Search Console does not break out AIO traffic, "clicks fell 12 percent after we lost the citation" cannot be verified from the data available and is exactly the sentence that ends up in a client deck. Co-occurrence is all the tracker can honestly report.

rule.statement: A query MAY enter the retrofit list only when `aio_present` was true in at least 5 of the 8 weeks and `our_domain_cited` was false in each of the last 4 weeks. The list MUST be ranked by the query's Search Console impressions for the window, and each entry MUST name the target URL and the domains cited instead.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope: 8-week trend view per query for retrofit prioritisation; widely established SEO prioritisation practice

rule.rationale: Retrofitting a page for a query whose panel appears two weeks in eight chases a SERP feature that is not stable for that query. Naming the domains currently cited is what tells the writer what the panel is drawing on.
